Definition: from G1722 and G2875; to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede, detain:--hinder, be tedious unto.
BiblicalUsage: To cut into, to hinder, to get in the way. Paul says Satan hindered him from coming to Thessalonica in 1 Thessalonians 2:18, husbands are warned that their prayers may be hindered in 1 Peter 3:7, and the Galatians were running well until someone hindered them from obeying the truth in Galatians 5:7.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hindrances come from every direction — Satan, sin, and even a careless marriage — and the race is won by those who notice the obstacle and refuse to stop. I hold that the truth is worth running for, and no hinderer gets the last word.
